questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨3,t,t⟩$, $q=⟨1,3,1⟩$, and $r=⟨1,1,3⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =\begin{vmatrix}3 & t & t \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =3\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix}-t\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix}+t\cdot \begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =3(3\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)-t(1\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)+t(1\cdot 1-3\cdot 1) \\  & =24-2t-2t \\  & =24-4t.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 24-4t & =0 \\ t & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=6.$

questions.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =\begin{vmatrix}k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =k\cdot \begin{vmatrix}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}-1\cdot \begin{vmatrix}8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix}+4\cdot \begin{vmatrix}8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =k(0\cdot 1-1\cdot 3)-(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 3)+4(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 0) \\  & =-3k+1+32 \\  & =33-3k \\  & =3(11-k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

questions.:question/problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,t,1⟩,$ $q=⟨3,2,6⟩,$ and $r=⟨3,4,0⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =\begin{vmatrix}t & t & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & 4 & 0\end{vmatrix} \\  & =t\cdot \begin{vmatrix}2 & 6 \\ 4 & 0\end{vmatrix}-t\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 6 \\ 3 & 0\end{vmatrix}+1\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =t(2\cdot 0-4\cdot 6)-t(3\cdot 0-3\cdot 6)+(3\cdot 4-3\cdot 2) \\  & =-24t+18t+6 \\  & =-6t+6 \\  & =6(1-t).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 6(1-t) & =0 \\ 1-t & =0 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=1.$

The first-row expansion of their scalar triple product is provided:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})&=k(0\cdot2-1\cdot1)\\
&\quad -(1\cdot2-1\cdot0)\\
&\quad +(1\cdot1-0\cdot0).
\end{aligned}
$$

Select the value of $k$.
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product is zero. Simplify the supplied expansion:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{b}\times\mathbf{c})&=k(0-1)-(2-0)+(1-0)\\
&=-k-2+1\\
&=-k-1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Set this equal to zero and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-k-1&=0\\
-k&=1\\
k&=-1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the vectors are coplanar exactly when $k=-1$. At this value the triple product is $-(-1)-1=0$, so the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors has zero volume.
